revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Refueling the Lander
revealWordProblem.text: A space-station crew has 27.6 liters of fuel to load into the lander. Each fuel cell holds exactly 3.45 liters. How many fuel cells can the crew completely fill? Make the divisor a whole number first, then divide.
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: 27.6 ÷ 3.45 = 8 fuel cells. Multiply both numbers by 100 to make the divisor whole: 2760 ÷ 345 = 8. Check: 8 × 3.45 = 27.6 liters.

conceptIntro.heading: How do you divide with decimals?
conceptIntro.intro: Dividing splits a total into equal groups. When you divide by a decimal, you first make the divisor (the number you divide by) a whole number, so the division is easier.
conceptIntro.keyIdea: Move the decimal point the same number of places in BOTH the divisor and the dividend; the answer stays the same.

iDo.title: Watch me
lines: I want 18.9 ÷ 6.3. The divisor is 6.3, and I want it to be a whole number.
I move the decimal point 1 place right in the divisor: 6.3 becomes 63.
I must move the dividend the same 1 place right: 18.9 becomes 189. Now the problem is 189 ÷ 63.
I check by multiplying: 6.3 × 3 = 18.9. Correct — 3 pods can be filled.

weDo.title: Let's try together
lines: Let's do 8.4 ÷ 2.1. How many places do we move to make 2.1 a whole number? (1 place, so 2.1 becomes 21.)
Move the dividend the same way: 8.4 becomes 84. What is the new problem? (84 ÷ 21.)

choiceFeedback: Re-read the problem carefully and try again.
Ten times too large — that happens when only 4.8 gets multiplied by 10. Scale both numbers the same way.
That looks like a subtraction (4.8 − 0.6) rather than a division. Reread the operation sign.
hints: Dividing by a decimal is easiest when the divisor is a whole number. Ask yourself what 0.6 needs to become.
Multiply the divisor and the dividend by the same power of 10. Here, multiplying by 10 does the job.
Multiplying both by 10 turns the problem into 48 ÷ 6. Carry out that division to finish.
hintsEs: Dividir entre un decimal es más fácil cuando el divisor es un número entero. Pregúntate en qué debe convertirse 0.6.
Multiplica el divisor y el dividendo por la misma potencia de 10. Aquí, multiplicar por 10 es suficiente.
Multiplicar ambos por 10 convierte el problema en 48 ÷ 6. Realiza esa división para terminar.

choiceFeedback: Re-read the problem carefully and try again.
The digits are right, but the value is 10 times too large. Recheck where the decimal point lands in the quotient.
That is nearly 9.45 itself, which would mean dividing by about 1. Since 0.9 is less than 1, the quotient has to be noticeably larger than 9.45.
hints: The divisor 0.9 is less than 1, so the quotient will be larger than 9.45. That is your size check.
Multiply the divisor and the dividend by the same power of 10 so the divisor becomes a whole number.
Multiplying both by 10 gives 94.5 ÷ 9. Divide, keeping the decimal point lined up.
hintsEs: El divisor 0.9 es menor que 1, así que el cociente será mayor que 9.45. Esa es tu comprobación de tamaño.
Multiplica el divisor y el dividendo por la misma potencia de 10 para que el divisor sea un número entero.
Multiplicar ambos por 10 da 94.5 ÷ 9. Divide manteniendo alineado el punto decimal.

optional.stem: A ribbon is 7.2 meters long and is cut into 0.8-meter pieces. How many pieces are there?
choiceFeedback: Re-read the problem carefully and try again.
Careful — the 7 comes from 7.2, not from dividing. Set up 72 ÷ 8 and work it out.
A little too high. Ten pieces of 0.8 meters would need 8 meters of ribbon, and you only have 7.2.
optional.stemEs: Un listón mide 7.2 metros de largo y se corta en pedazos de 0.8 metros. ¿Cuántos pedazos hay?
hints: Cutting a length into equal pieces is a division: total length ÷ length of one piece.
Make the divisor a whole number by multiplying both 7.2 and 0.8 by 10.
That turns the problem into 72 ÷ 8. Count how many 8s fit into 72.
hintsEs: Cortar una longitud en pedazos iguales es una división: longitud total ÷ longitud de un pedazo.
Convierte el divisor en número entero multiplicando 7.2 y 0.8 por 10.
Eso convierte el problema en 72 ÷ 8. Cuenta cuántos 8 caben en 72.

optional.explanation: Dividing by 0.25 is like multiplying by 4: 15 × 4 = 60.
choiceFeedback: Multiply the whole numbers first, then count decimal places.
That is 15 ÷ 10. Dividing by 0.25 is not the same as sliding the decimal point one place.
Dividing by a number less than 1 makes the result larger, not smaller. 0.6 is far below 15.
optional.explanationEs: Dividir entre 0.25 es lo mismo que multiplicar por 4: 15 × 4 = 60.
hints: Think about how many quarters fit inside one whole — 0.25 is one quarter.
If four 0.25s fit in every 1, then dividing by 0.25 does the same job as multiplying by 4.
So the problem becomes 15 × 4. Work that product out.
hintsEs: Piensa cuántos cuartos caben en un entero: 0.25 es un cuarto.
Si cuatro veces 0.25 caben en cada 1, entonces dividir entre 0.25 hace lo mismo que multiplicar por 4.
Así el problema se convierte en 15 × 4. Calcula ese producto.

optional.stem: Table 1 splits a $15.00 lunch bill equally among 4 friends. How much does each friend pay?
choiceFeedback: Re-read the problem carefully and try again.
That is more than a quarter of $15.00. Four payments of $5.30 would come to over $21.
This is larger than the whole bill, so it cannot be one person's share. Divide by 4 instead of multiplying.
optional.stemEs: La mesa 1 divide en partes iguales una cuenta de almuerzo de $15.00 entre 4 amigos. ¿Cuánto paga cada amigo?
hints: Splitting a bill equally means dividing the total by the number of people.
Set up 15.00 ÷ 4. The divisor is already a whole number, so no scaling is needed.
4 goes into 15 three times with 3 left over. Bring down the decimal digits and keep dividing.
hintsEs: Dividir una cuenta en partes iguales significa dividir el total entre el número de personas.
Plantea 15.00 ÷ 4. El divisor ya es un número entero, así que no hace falta escalar.
El 4 cabe tres veces en 15 y sobran 3. Baja las cifras decimales y sigue dividiendo.

optional.stem: A recipe uses 9.6 cups of flour to make 3 equal batches of muffins. How many cups of flour go in each batch?
choiceFeedback: Re-read the problem carefully and try again.
The digits are right, but 32 cups is far more than you started with. Check where the decimal point belongs in the quotient.
That looks like 9.6 - 3. The word 'each' here signals division, not subtraction.
optional.stemEs: Una receta usa 9.6 tazas de harina para hacer 3 tandas iguales de panecillos. ¿Cuántas tazas de harina lleva cada tanda?
hints: Equal batches means the flour is shared evenly, so this is a division.
Divide the total flour by the number of batches: 9.6 ÷ 3.
3 goes into 9 three times; then bring down the .6 and keep going.
hintsEs: Tandas iguales significa que la harina se reparte por igual, así que esto es una división.
Divide la harina total entre el número de tandas: 9.6 ÷ 3.
El 3 cabe tres veces en 9; después baja el .6 y continúa.

optional.stem: The arcade corner has 8.1 meters of token ribbon, cut into 0.9-meter prize strips. How many strips can the cafe make?
choiceFeedback: Re-read the problem carefully and try again.
Ten times too many — that happens when only 8.1 is multiplied by 10. Scale both numbers together.
8.1 is the total length in meters, not the number of strips. You still need to divide it by 0.9.
optional.stemEs: El rincón de videojuegos tiene 8.1 metros de listón de fichas, que se corta en tiras de premio de 0.9 metros. ¿Cuántas tiras puede hacer el café?
hints: How many 0.9-meter pieces fit inside 8.1 meters? That question is a division.
Multiply both 8.1 and 0.9 by 10 so the divisor becomes a whole number.
The problem becomes 81 ÷ 9. Finish the division from there.
hintsEs: ¿Cuántos pedazos de 0.9 metros caben en 8.1 metros? Esa pregunta es una división.
Multiplica 8.1 y 0.9 por 10 para que el divisor sea un número entero.
El problema se convierte en 81 ÷ 9. Termina la división desde ahí.

optional.label: Match each cafe order to its quotient to unlock the table number.
optional.explanation: Each order becomes an easy whole-number division after the divisor is shifted: 84 ÷ 6 = 14, 75 ÷ 25 = 3, 504 ÷ 12 = 42, 112 ÷ 14 = 8, and 63 ÷ 9 = 7. The first order already has a whole-number divisor, so $12.50 ÷ 5 = $2.50 needs no shifting at all.
optional.explanationEs: Cada pedido se convierte en una división sencilla con números enteros después de mover el divisor: 84 ÷ 6 = 14, 75 ÷ 25 = 3, 504 ÷ 12 = 42, 112 ÷ 14 = 8 y 63 ÷ 9 = 7. El primer pedido ya tiene un divisor entero, así que $12.50 ÷ 5 = $2.50 no necesita ningún cambio.
hints: Every order divides a decimal amount by another number, and the quotient stays the same only if you shift both numbers the same way.
Check the divisor in each order first: 5 is already whole, 0.6, 2.5, 1.4, and 0.9 each need ×10, and 0.12 needs ×100.
Start with 8.4 ÷ 0.6: multiply both by 10 to get 84 ÷ 6, then look for the quotient card that fits.
hintsEs: Cada pedido divide una cantidad decimal entre otro número, y el cociente se mantiene igual solo si mueves los dos números de la misma manera.
Revisa primero el divisor de cada pedido: 5 ya es entero; 0.6, 2.5, 1.4 y 0.9 necesitan ×10, y 0.12 necesita ×100.
Empieza con 8.4 ÷ 0.6: multiplica los dos por 10 para obtener 84 ÷ 6 y luego busca la tarjeta del cociente que corresponde.
optional.labelEs: Une cada pedido de la cafetería con su cociente para descubrir el número de mesa.

optional.title: Level 2 Extension — The Misplaced Decimal at the Register

workedExample.label: Order
workedExample.work: A $13.50 catering tray is split into 0.45-pound scoops. How many scoops?

optional.correctWork: Moving both points 2 places gives 1350 ÷ 45, which equals 30, not 3.0 — the decimal point was placed one spot too far left. So 13.50 ÷ 0.45 = 30 scoops. Check: 30 × 0.45 = 13.50. ✓
hints: After you rewrite it as 1350 ÷ 45, estimate first: about how many 45s fit in 1350? That is much more than 3.
1350 ÷ 45 = 30. The cashier slid the decimal one place too far left, turning 30 into 3.0.
optional.titleEs: Extensión de Nivel 2: el punto decimal mal colocado en la caja
optional.explanation: The rewrite to 1350 ÷ 45 was done correctly, but the final step placed the decimal point one spot too far left. Since 45 × 30 = 1,350, the answer is 30 scoops, not 3.0, and 30 × 0.45 = 13.50 confirms it.
optional.explanationEs: La reescritura a 1350 ÷ 45 se hizo correctamente, pero el paso final colocó el punto decimal un lugar demasiado a la izquierda. Como 45 × 30 = 1,350, la respuesta es 30 porciones, no 3.0, y 30 × 0.45 = 13.50 lo confirma.

choiceFeedback: Re-read the problem carefully and try again.
That result is 10 times too large — a sign the decimal point moved in only one of the numbers. Scale the dividend and the divisor by the same power of 10.
The decimal point slid in the wrong direction. Since 1.2 fits into 14.4 more than once, the quotient has to be greater than 1.
hints: Dividing by a decimal is awkward — notice the divisor 1.2 has one decimal place. There's a move that makes it whole.
Multiply BOTH numbers by 10: scaling dividend and divisor the same way keeps the quotient exactly the same.
Compute 14.4 × 10 = 144 and 1.2 × 10 = 12. Now solve 144 ÷ 12 — a whole-number division you already know how to do.
hintsEs: Dividir entre un decimal es incómodo: fíjate que el divisor 1.2 tiene un lugar decimal. Hay un movimiento que lo vuelve entero.
Multiplica AMBOS números por 10: escalar el dividendo y el divisor igual deja el cociente exactamente igual.
Calcula 14.4 × 10 = 144 y 1.2 × 10 = 12. Ahora resuelve 144 ÷ 12, una división de enteros que ya sabes hacer.

choiceFeedback: Re-read the problem carefully and try again.
Your digits are right, but the decimal point is one place too far left. Since 0.6 is less than 1, the quotient must be greater than 3.78.
The digits are right, but the decimal point moved two places the wrong way. Dividing by a number less than 1 gives a quotient larger than the number you started with.
hints: The divisor 0.6 has one decimal place — shifting both numbers one place makes the divisor a whole number.
Multiply both numbers by 10 to build an equivalent problem, then divide, keeping the decimal point in the dividend.
3.78 × 10 = 37.8 and 0.6 × 10 = 6. Now compute 37.8 ÷ 6, keeping the decimal point lined up in your answer.
hintsEs: El divisor 0.6 tiene un lugar decimal: mover ambos números un lugar convierte al divisor en entero.
Multiplica ambos números por 10 para armar un problema equivalente y luego divide, cuidando el punto decimal del dividendo.
3.78 × 10 = 37.8 y 0.6 × 10 = 6. Ahora calcula 37.8 ÷ 6, manteniendo el punto decimal alineado en tu respuesta.

choiceFeedback: Re-read the problem carefully and try again.
You multiplied 8.4 by 10 but left 0.7 alone. Both numbers have to grow by the same factor for the quotient to stay the same.
The decimal point went the wrong way. 0.7 fits into 8.4 many times, so the quotient is much larger than 1.
hints: Ask yourself: how many groups of 0.7 fit inside 8.4? Since 0.7 is less than 1, expect MORE groups than 8.
Scale both numbers by 10 so you're dividing by a whole number instead of a decimal.
8.4 becomes 84 and 0.7 becomes 7. Solve 84 ÷ 7 — your 7s times-table facts will carry you there.
hintsEs: Pregúntate: ¿cuántos grupos de 0.7 caben en 8.4? Como 0.7 es menor que 1, espera MÁS de 8 grupos.
Escala ambos números por 10 para dividir entre un número entero en lugar de un decimal.
8.4 se vuelve 84 y 0.7 se vuelve 7. Resuelve 84 ÷ 7: la tabla del 7 te lleva directo.

approaching.label: Rewrite each problem by making the divisor a whole number, then solve.
hints: The 'Multiply Both By' column is the key move: choose 10 or 100 based on how many decimal places the DIVISOR has.
One decimal place in the divisor means multiply both numbers by 10; then rewrite and divide whole numbers.
Row 1: 0.9 has one decimal place, so multiply 4.5 and 0.9 each by 10 and write the new whole-number problem in the row.
approaching.explanation: Multiplying the dividend and the divisor by the same power of 10 slides both decimal points without changing the quotient. Each divisor here has one decimal place, so ×10 rewrites 4.5 ÷ 0.9 as 45 ÷ 9 = 5 and 3.6 ÷ 0.4 as 36 ÷ 4 = 9.
approaching.explanationEs: Multiplicar el dividendo y el divisor por la misma potencia de 10 mueve los dos puntos decimales sin cambiar el cociente. Aquí cada divisor tiene un lugar decimal, así que ×10 reescribe 4.5 ÷ 0.9 como 45 ÷ 9 = 5 y 3.6 ÷ 0.4 como 36 ÷ 4 = 9.
approaching.labelEs: Reescribe cada problema convirtiendo el divisor en un número entero y después resuelve.
hintsEs: La columna 'Multiplicar Ambos Por' es el movimiento clave: elige 10 o 100 según cuántos decimales tenga el DIVISOR.
Un decimal en el divisor significa multiplicar ambos números por 10; luego reescribe y divide números enteros.
Fila 1: 0.9 tiene un lugar decimal, así que multiplica 4.5 y 0.9 por 10 y escribe el nuevo problema de enteros en la fila.

choiceFeedback: Re-read the problem carefully and try again.
This result is 10 times too large. Check that you multiplied both 15.6 and 1.3 by the same power of 10 before dividing.
13 is the divisor after scaling, not the quotient. You still have to divide 156 by 13.
hints: The divisor 1.3 isn't a whole number — shift both numbers before you divide anything.
Multiply dividend and divisor by 10, then divide. Check at the end: your answer times 1.3 should rebuild 15.6.
15.6 × 10 = 156 and 1.3 × 10 = 13. Now count how many 13s fit into 156 — start by trying 13 × 10.
hintsEs: El divisor 1.3 no es entero: mueve ambos números antes de dividir nada.
Multiplica dividendo y divisor por 10 y luego divide. Comprueba al final: tu respuesta por 1.3 debe reconstruir 15.6.
15.6 × 10 = 156 y 1.3 × 10 = 13. Ahora cuenta cuántos 13 caben en 156; empieza probando 13 × 10.

approaching.title: Spot the Common Mistake
approaching.correctWork: The student moved the decimal point in the divisor (0.8 → 8) but forgot to move it the same 1 place in the dividend. You must move BOTH: 6.4 becomes 64, so 64 ÷ 8 = 8. So 6.4 ÷ 0.8 = 8. Check: 8 × 0.8 = 6.4. ✓
hints: When you moved 0.8 to 8, what did you have to do to 6.4 as well?
Move the decimal the same 1 place in both: 6.4 → 64, then 64 ÷ 8 = 8.
approaching.explanation: In the last step 6.4 was divided by the new whole-number divisor without being shifted itself. Both numbers have to move the same 1 place, so 6.4 becomes 64 and the problem is 64 ÷ 8 = 8. Checking confirms it: 8 × 0.8 = 6.4.
approaching.explanationEs: En el último paso se dividió 6.4 entre el nuevo divisor entero sin moverlo también. Los dos números tienen que moverse el mismo 1 lugar, así que 6.4 se convierte en 64 y el problema es 64 ÷ 8 = 8. La comprobación lo confirma: 8 × 0.8 = 6.4.

onLevel.label: Solve each decimal division problem.
hints: Every row uses the same move: shift both numbers until the divisor is whole, then divide as usual.
Count the divisor's decimal places to pick ×10 or ×100 — a divisor like 0.24 needs ×100 — then divide the new whole numbers.
Row 1: 9.6 ÷ 0.8 becomes 96 ÷ 8 after multiplying both by 10. Solve that, then apply the same shift to every other row.
onLevel.explanation: Once the divisor is shifted to a whole number, each row is ordinary division: 96 ÷ 8 = 12, 156 ÷ 13 = 12, 245 ÷ 35 = 7, and 576 ÷ 24 = 24 (that row needs ×100 because 0.24 has two decimal places). The last row becomes 113.4 ÷ 9 = 12.6, since only the divisor has to end up whole.
onLevel.explanationEs: Una vez que el divisor se convierte en entero, cada fila es una división común: 96 ÷ 8 = 12, 156 ÷ 13 = 12, 245 ÷ 35 = 7 y 576 ÷ 24 = 24 (esa fila necesita ×100 porque 0.24 tiene dos lugares decimales). La última fila queda como 113.4 ÷ 9 = 12.6, ya que solo el divisor tiene que quedar entero.
onLevel.labelEs: Resuelve cada problema de división de decimales.
hintsEs: Cada fila usa el mismo movimiento: mueve ambos números hasta que el divisor sea entero y luego divide normalmente.
Cuenta los decimales del divisor para elegir ×10 o ×100 — un divisor como 0.24 necesita ×100 — y luego divide los nuevos enteros.
Fila 1: 9.6 ÷ 0.8 se vuelve 96 ÷ 8 al multiplicar ambos por 10. Resuélvelo y aplica el mismo cambio en todas las demás filas.

onLevel.label: Match each decimal division to its quotient.
hints: Shift both numbers in each problem until the divisor is whole — most of these turn into basic division facts.
Estimate sizes too: dividing by a number less than 1 gives a quotient BIGGER than the dividend itself.
Try 7.2 ÷ 0.8: times 10 turns it into 72 ÷ 8, a times-table fact. Match it, then shift each remaining problem the same way.
onLevel.explanation: Shifting each divisor to a whole number turns every match into simple division: 72 ÷ 8 = 9, 45.6 ÷ 6 = 7.6, 132 ÷ 12 = 11, 360 ÷ 12 = 30, 105 ÷ 15 = 7, and 9.6 ÷ 8 = 1.2. Notice that dividing by a number smaller than 1, such as 0.12, gives a quotient larger than the dividend.
onLevel.explanationEs: Convertir cada divisor en entero transforma cada pareja en una división sencilla: 72 ÷ 8 = 9, 45.6 ÷ 6 = 7.6, 132 ÷ 12 = 11, 360 ÷ 12 = 30, 105 ÷ 15 = 7 y 9.6 ÷ 8 = 1.2. Fíjate en que dividir entre un número menor que 1, como 0.12, da un cociente mayor que el dividendo.
onLevel.labelEs: Une cada división de decimales con su cociente.
hintsEs: Mueve ambos números de cada problema hasta que el divisor sea entero: casi todos se convierten en hechos básicos de división.
Estima también los tamaños: dividir entre un número menor que 1 da un cociente MAYOR que el dividendo mismo.
Prueba 7.2 ÷ 0.8: por 10 se vuelve 72 ÷ 8, un dato de la tabla. Únelo y mueve cada problema restante igual.

onLevel.stem: A water tank holds 19.2 liters. It is poured into bottles that each hold 1.6 liters. How many bottles can be filled?
choiceFeedback: Multiply the whole numbers first, then count decimal places.
That is one bottle more than the division gives. Multiply both numbers by 10 and divide 192 by 16 carefully — it comes out even, with nothing left over.
The digits look right—how many total decimal places should the product have?
hints: You're asking how many 1.6s fit into 19.2 — that's division, and the divisor 1.6 needs to become whole first.
Multiply both amounts by 10 to build an equivalent whole-number division, then divide.
19.2 × 10 = 192 and 1.6 × 10 = 16. Now divide 192 by 16 — start by taking out the chunk 16 × 10 = 160.
onLevel.stemEs: Un tanque de agua contiene 19.2 litros. Se vacía en botellas que contienen 1.6 litros cada una. ¿Cuántas botellas se pueden llenar?
hintsEs: Estás preguntando cuántos 1.6 caben en 19.2: eso es división, y el divisor 1.6 debe volverse entero primero.
Multiplica ambas cantidades por 10 para armar una división equivalente de enteros y luego divide.
19.2 × 10 = 192 y 1.6 × 10 = 16. Ahora divide 192 entre 16; empieza sacando el bloque 16 × 10 = 160.

onLevel.instructions: Sort: should you multiply both numbers by 10 or by 100 to make the divisor a whole number?
hints: Look ONLY at the divisor — the second number in each problem. Count its decimal places; that count makes the decision.
One decimal place in the divisor (like 0.7 or 2.1) means ×10. Two places (like 0.12 or 0.36) means ×100.
Take '6.3 ÷ 0.7': the divisor 0.7 has one decimal place, so it needs ×10. Place it, then count places on each remaining divisor.
onLevel.explanation: Only the divisor decides the shift, because the whole point of the move is to make the divisor a whole number. The divisors 0.7, 2.1, and 1.7 have one decimal place, so those problems go in the ×10 group, while 0.12, 0.36, and 0.15 have two decimal places and belong in the ×100 group.
onLevel.explanationEs: Solo el divisor decide el cambio, porque el objetivo del movimiento es convertir el divisor en un número entero. Los divisores 0.7, 2.1 y 1.7 tienen un lugar decimal, así que esos problemas van en el grupo de ×10, mientras que 0.12, 0.36 y 0.15 tienen dos lugares decimales y pertenecen al grupo de ×100.
onLevel.instructionsEs: Clasifica: ¿debes multiplicar los dos números por 10 o por 100 para convertir el divisor en un número entero?
hintsEs: Mira SOLO el divisor, el segundo número de cada problema. Cuenta sus decimales: esa cantidad decide todo.
Un decimal en el divisor (como 0.7 o 2.1) significa ×10. Dos decimales (como 0.12 o 0.36) significan ×100.
Toma '6.3 ÷ 0.7': el divisor 0.7 tiene un lugar decimal, así que necesita ×10. Colócalo y cuenta los decimales de cada divisor restante.

onLevel.title: Spot the Common Mistake

workedExample.label: Count how far to move
workedExample.work: 0.12 has 2 decimal places, so BOTH numbers move 2 places right. The divisor: 0.12 → 12.

workedExample.label: Move the dividend the same 2 places
workedExample.work: 9.6 only has one digit after the point, so the student moved it just 1 place: 9.6 → 96. New problem: 96 ÷ 12 = 8.

onLevel.correctWork: Both numbers must move the SAME number of places — 2, not 1. 9.6 runs out of digits after one place, so you add a placeholder zero to move the second place: 9.6 → 96 → 960. The real problem is 960 ÷ 12 = 80, so 9.6 ÷ 0.12 = 80. Estimate to confirm: 0.12 is tiny, so many of them fit in 9.6 — the quotient must be large, not 8. Check: 80 × 0.12 = 9.6. ✓
hints: The divisor moved 2 places (0.12 → 12), so the dividend has to move 2 places too — the student only moved it 1.
9.6 has no second digit to move, so add a placeholder zero: 9.6 → 960. Then 960 ÷ 12 = 80.
onLevel.explanation: In the last step the dividend moved only 1 place while the divisor moved 2, so the two numbers no longer match. Adding a placeholder zero lets 9.6 move both places to 960, making the real problem 960 ÷ 12 = 80. That size is reasonable, because a great many 0.12s fit inside 9.6.
onLevel.explanationEs: En el último paso el dividendo se movió solo 1 lugar mientras que el divisor se movió 2, así que los dos números ya no coinciden. Agregar un cero de relleno permite que 9.6 se mueva los dos lugares hasta 960, y el problema real es 960 ÷ 12 = 80. Ese tamaño tiene sentido, porque muchísimos 0.12 caben dentro de 9.6.

extending.title: Find Derek's Mistake
extending.correctWork: Derek only multiplied by 10, but the divisor 0.45 has two decimal places. He should multiply both numbers by 100: 720 ÷ 45 = 16. He got the right answer by luck this time, but his method is unreliable because the divisor is still a decimal (4.5).
hints: How many decimal places does 0.45 have? Did Derek multiply by enough to make it a whole number?
0.45 has two decimal places, so multiply both by 100, not 10. 0.45 × 100 = 45 and 7.2 × 100 = 720.
extending.explanation: In the step where Derek multiplied by 10, the divisor only became 4.5 — still a decimal, so the setup was never finished. Because 0.45 has two decimal places, both numbers need ×100, giving 720 ÷ 45 = 16. The quotient does not change, but leaving a decimal divisor makes the long division far harder than it needs to be.
extending.explanationEs: En el paso donde Derek multiplicó por 10, el divisor solo llegó a 4.5, que sigue siendo un decimal, así que el planteamiento nunca se terminó. Como 0.45 tiene dos lugares decimales, los dos números necesitan ×100, lo que da 720 ÷ 45 = 16. El cociente no cambia, pero dejar un divisor decimal vuelve la división mucho más difícil de lo necesario.

extending.prompt: A gas station sells fuel at $3.45 per gallon. A customer pays $27.60 total. How many gallons did the customer buy? Set up the decimal division, show how to convert it to whole-number division, and solve.
extending.sentenceFrame: The equation is $27.60 ÷ $3.45 = ___. I multiply both by ___ to get ___ ÷ ___ = ___ gallons.
hints: Total money ÷ price per gallon = gallons, so set up 27.60 ÷ 3.45 — and notice the divisor has TWO decimal places.
Multiply both numbers by 100 so the divisor becomes a whole number, then divide the two new whole numbers.
27.60 × 100 = 2,760 and 3.45 × 100 = 345. Now ask how many 345s fit into 2,760 — note that 345 × 10 = 3,450 is already too big.
extending.explanation: Total cost divided by price per gallon gives the number of gallons, so the setup is 27.60 ÷ 3.45. The divisor has two decimal places, so multiplying both numbers by 100 gives 2,760 ÷ 345 = 8 gallons, and 8 × $3.45 = $27.60 confirms it.
extending.explanationEs: El costo total dividido entre el precio por galón da la cantidad de galones, así que el planteamiento es 27.60 ÷ 3.45. El divisor tiene dos lugares decimales, así que multiplicar los dos números por 100 da 2,760 ÷ 345 = 8 galones, y 8 × $3.45 = $27.60 lo confirma.
extending.promptEs: Una gasolinera vende combustible a $3.45 por galón. Un cliente paga $27.60 en total. ¿Cuántos galones compró? Plantea la división de decimales, muestra cómo convertirla en una división de números enteros y resuelve.
hintsEs: Dinero total ÷ precio por galón = galones, así que plantea 27.60 ÷ 3.45, y fíjate que el divisor tiene DOS decimales.
Multiplica ambos números por 100 para que el divisor sea entero y luego divide los dos números nuevos.
27.60 × 100 = 2,760 y 3.45 × 100 = 345. Ahora pregunta cuántos 345 caben en 2,760; nota que 345 × 10 = 3,450 ya es demasiado.

extending.instructions: Verify each division by showing that quotient × divisor = dividend. Are the two sides balanced?
hints: A balanced scale says the same thing twice: quotient × divisor must rebuild the dividend exactly.
Multiply out the right side of each scale and compare it to the left side's dividend — any mismatch means unbalanced.
First scale: does 12 × 0.8 really equal 9.6? Compute 12 × 8 = 96, give it one decimal place, and compare with the left side.
extending.explanation: A division is correct only when quotient × divisor rebuilds the dividend. 12 × 0.8 = 9.6 and 63 × 0.12 = 7.56 both match their dividends, so those two scales balance, but 5 × 0.9 = 4.5 instead of 5.4, so the third one tips — the true quotient is 6, since 6 × 0.9 = 5.4.
extending.explanationEs: Una división es correcta solo cuando cociente × divisor reconstruye el dividendo. 12 × 0.8 = 9.6 y 63 × 0.12 = 7.56 coinciden con sus dividendos, así que esas dos balanzas quedan equilibradas, pero 5 × 0.9 = 4.5 en vez de 5.4, así que la tercera se desequilibra: el cociente verdadero es 6, ya que 6 × 0.9 = 5.4.

practice.commonMistake: A common mistake in Divide Decimals is moving the decimal point in the divisor but forgetting to move it the same number of places in the dividend. For example, in 6.4 ÷ 0.8 a student changes 0.8 to 8 but leaves the dividend as 6.4, then divides 6.4 ÷ 8 = 0.8 instead of moving both points to get 64 ÷ 8 = 8. A second version of this mistake happens when the divisor has two decimal places, like 0.12: students move both points only 1 place instead of 2, turning 9.6 ÷ 0.12 into 96 ÷ 1.2 instead of the correct 960 ÷ 12. Count the divisor's decimal places first, then move BOTH points that same number of places.

connect.scenario: A ribbon is 16.8 feet long. You need to cut it into pieces that are each 2.4 feet long for a craft project.
connect.promptQuestion: How does decimal division help you figure out how many pieces you can cut?

exitTicket.hint: Think through the problem step by step.
choiceFeedback: Move both decimals so you divide by a whole number, then divide.
Check your decimal placement — you shifted one place too many.
Dividing by less than 1 makes the answer larger, not smaller.
hints: Notice the divisor 0.8 has one decimal place — that tells you exactly how far to shift both numbers.
Multiply both 19.2 and 0.8 by 10 to create an equivalent division with a whole-number divisor.
That gives 192 ÷ 8. Break it apart: 160 ÷ 8 = 20, then divide the leftover 32 by 8 and combine your two pieces.

34 × 26 = 884. There are 2 total decimal places (1 + 1), so place the decimal to get 8.84.
Round 4.8 to 5 and 3.2 to 3. The estimate 5 × 3 = 15 is closest to the exact answer 15.36.
